metadata.name: Picnic Like a Pro
metadata.description: CALM architecture of the Picnic Like a Pro Telegram grocery and meal-planning assistant.

nodes.name: Family member
nodes.description: A person in ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS chatting with the bot from their own Telegram account. All family members share one Picnic account (one cart, one order history).

nodes.name: Operator
nodes.description: Whoever runs the deployment: owns .env, runs migrations and the maintenance scripts, triggers deploys, and receives Picnic's 2FA codes.

nodes.name: Telegram Bot API
nodes.description: Telegram's cloud. Users message the bot there; the bot fetches updates by long polling.

nodes.name: OpenRouter
nodes.description: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions gateway in front of every LLM provider; the model is chosen per chat.

nodes.name: Picnic API
nodes.description: Picnic's private storefront API (NL/DE/BE), reached through the python-picnic-api2 library. Search, cart, delivery slots, deliveries, articles, login + 2FA.

nodes.name: External MCP client
nodes.description: Optional: Claude Desktop or any other MCP client talking to the standalone MCP server (uv run mcp-server).

nodes.name: GitHub Actions
nodes.description: CI (tests.yml: pytest + docker build checks) and the manual Build & Deploy workflow (deploy.yml).

nodes.name: GitHub Container Registry
nodes.description: Holds the production image ghcr.io/<repo>:latest and :<sha>.

nodes.name: VPS Docker host
nodes.description: The operator's server. Runs docker compose; no inbound ports are opened for the bot.

nodes.name: picnic-bot container
nodes.description: The runtime stage of the Dockerfile; ENTRYPOINT `uv run`, CMD `bot`. Named volume picnic-data mounted at /app/data. The maintenance scripts are run inside it with `docker compose exec`.

nodes.name: Picnic Like a Pro
nodes.description: Family grocery and meal-planning assistant: a Telegram bot that answers through an LLM with MCP tools over the Picnic API and a local SQLite order history.

nodes.name: Telegram bot
nodes.description: Entry point (`uv run bot`). Command handlers, allowlist checks, and the tool-use loop `_run_llm`: fetch context, call the LLM, execute tool calls, commit the turn only if it ended cleanly. Refuses to start when the schema is behind (SchemaOutOfDateError).

telegram-user-allowlist.description: Every handler checks the sender against ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS; an empty list denies everyone unless ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true. This is the only control protecting stored conversations.

config.name: Telegram user allowlist
config.description: Every handler checks the sender against ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS; an empty list denies everyone unless ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true. This is the only control protecting stored conversations.
config.allowed-principals: Telegram user ids in ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS (everyone if ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true)
config.enforced-in: src/picnic_meal_planner/access.py::is_allowed, called by every handler in bot.py

picnic-login-authorisation.description: /picnic_login and /picnic_code are further restricted to PICNIC_LOGIN_USER_IDS, because each login texts the account owner a code.

config.name: Picnic login authorisation
config.description: /picnic_login and /picnic_code are further restricted to PICNIC_LOGIN_USER_IDS, because each login texts the account owner a code.
config.allowed-principals: PICNIC_LOGIN_USER_IDS, a subset of the allowed users (all of them when unset)

clean-turn-archiving.description: A turn whose last assistant message has an unanswered tool_use or empty content is discarded, never stored, so one bad completion cannot poison the chat.

config.name: Only clean turns are archived
config.description: A turn whose last assistant message has an unanswered tool_use or empty content is discarded, never stored, so one bad completion cannot poison the chat.
config.failure-mode: Turn discarded and the user asked to retry

nodes.name: LLM gateway
nodes.description: OpenRouter client. Translates the Anthropic-shaped history (text / tool_use / tool_result) to the OpenAI wire format and back on every request, and resolves the per-chat model (chat_settings.model, else LLM_MODEL).

model-allowlist.description: set_chat_model rejects models not in LLM_ALLOWED_MODELS (empty = any).

config.name: LLM model allowlist
config.description: set_chat_model rejects models not in LLM_ALLOWED_MODELS (empty = any).
config.allowed-principals: Model ids in LLM_ALLOWED_MODELS (any model when unset)

nodes.name: API logger
nodes.description: Best-effort, replayable log of every Picnic and OpenRouter HTTP call: method, full URL, headers and untruncated bodies, with credentials masked. Picnic is captured by wrapping the library's requests.Session; OpenRouter by llm.create_message. A contextvar request_context groups rows per bot turn or script run and carries the chat's consent decision.

api-log-best-effort.description: Persisting a row never changes the outcome of the logged request. Rows are written on a separate engine with a 0.2 s lock timeout.

config.name: API logging never affects the request
config.description: Persisting a row never changes the outcome of the logged request. Rows are written on a separate engine with a 0.2 s lock timeout.
config.failure-mode: Warning and a lost row; separate engine with a 0.2 s lock timeout so a locked DB does not stall API calls

api-log-redaction.description: Authorization, x-picnic-auth, cookies and token/secret/api-key headers, and password/secret/otp/token body keys, are stored as [REDACTED].

config.name: Credential redaction in the API log
config.description: Authorization, x-picnic-auth, cookies and token/secret/api-key headers, and password/secret/otp/token body keys, are stored as [REDACTED].
config.erasure: Credential header values and body keys are replaced by [REDACTED] before storage
config.failure-mode: best-effort log: a failed write loses the row, never the request

nodes.name: Conversation history
nodes.description: All history policy: per-chat in-memory window, turn-aware loading and trimming, persistence, opt-out, deletion by chat/turn/day. bot.py only calls get_context() and commit_turn().

history-consent.description: Storage is opt-out per chat (/privacy off also deletes what is stored) and globally (PERSIST_CONVERSATIONS=false). The consent check fails closed on DB errors; deletions propagate errors.

config.name: Conversation storage consent
config.description: Storage is opt-out per chat (/privacy off also deletes what is stored) and globally (PERSIST_CONVERSATIONS=false). The consent check fails closed on DB errors; deletions propagate errors.
config.erasure: /privacy off deletes and stops storing; PERSIST_CONVERSATIONS=false stores nothing

turn-integrity.description: A turn is the unit of deletion and the API window never opens mid-turn, so no tool_result is ever orphaned (which would 400 every later request).

config.name: Turn-aware history window
config.description: A turn is the unit of deletion and the API window never opens mid-turn, so no tool_result is ever orphaned (which would 400 every later request).
config.failure-mode: Drop whole turns (never truncate one); return [] if no safe boundary

nodes.name: MCP tool server
nodes.description: FastMCP server with 15 tools (Picnic, order history, forecasting). The bot calls the tools in-process via get_tool_schemas()/call_tool(); `uv run mcp-server` exposes the same tools over stdio, SSE or streamable HTTP. Tool exceptions become {"error": str(exc)} results.

destructive-cart-confirmation.description: clear_cart only acts with confirm=true. add_to_cart / remove_from_cart rely on the system prompt telling the model to confirm with the user first.

config.name: Confirm cart changes
config.description: clear_cart only acts with confirm=true. add_to_cart / remove_from_cart rely on the system prompt telling the model to confirm with the user first.

nodes.name: Picnic client
nodes.description: Async wrapper around the synchronous python-picnic-api2 (thread-pool executor), converting pydantic models to dicts. auth.py owns the session-token-first login policy and the 2FA LoginFlow; _call() keeps the stored token current, turns a rejected token into PicnicLoginRequired, and a 429 or an HTML 403 into PicnicRateLimited. Category lookups read the product page and the L2 category page. Every HTTP call is captured by api_log. PICNIC_MOCK=true swaps in the mock.

no-unprompted-2fa.description: A password login that hits 2FA raises PicnicLoginRequired instead of requesting a code; only an explicit /picnic_login or scripts/picnic_login.py sends one. A pending login blocks every other password login for its 10-minute TTL.

config.name: No unprompted Picnic 2FA codes
config.description: A password login that hits 2FA raises PicnicLoginRequired instead of requesting a code; only an explicit /picnic_login or scripts/picnic_login.py sends one. A pending login blocks every other password login for its 10-minute TTL.
config.failure-mode: PicnicLoginRequired / PicnicLoginPending surfaced as a tool error

nodes.name: Mock Picnic API
nodes.description: In-process fake of PicnicAPI: ~50 products, stateful cart, delivery slots and 25 generated weekly deliveries. Used by the mock environment, CI and every test.

nodes.name: Forecasting engine
nodes.description: Pure-Python average-interval model: urgency = days since last order / average interval. No I/O.

nodes.name: Database access layer
nodes.description: SQLAlchemy 2.0 async engine and session factory (PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every connection), ORM models, and commit-neutral query helpers that return plain dicts. Two engines on the same file: get_db() for everything and get_log_db() with a 0.2 s lock timeout for the API log. Startup gate: ensure_schema() (pending_migration, init_db, missing_columns).

schema-version-gate.description: The bot, MCP server, import script and web app refuse to run when Alembic's revision is behind SCHEMA_REVISION (checked before init_db) or when columns are missing.

config.name: Schema version gate
config.description: The bot, MCP server, import script and web app refuse to run when Alembic's revision is behind SCHEMA_REVISION (checked before init_db) or when columns are missing.

nodes.name: SQLite database
nodes.description: A single SQLite file (DB_PATH, default data/picnic.db) on the picnic-data volume; shared by the bot and every script. Schema managed by Alembic (0001-0011).

nodes.name: Order history and product catalogue
nodes.description: Tables products, categories, category_parents, orders, order_items and import_checkpoints: every imported or recorded delivery with prices, and Picnic's categories, which hold the only copy of each category name.

nodes.name: Conversation transcripts
nodes.description: Table conversation_messages: the full per-chat transcript (only the API window is capped), grouped by turn_id.

retention-and-erasure.description: /forget deletes a chat's rows; /privacy off deletes and stops storing. Retention is otherwise unbounded and the file is unencrypted (see OPEN_POINTS.md 1.3/1.4).

config.name: Transcript retention and erasure
config.description: /forget deletes a chat's rows; /privacy off deletes and stops storing. Retention is otherwise unbounded and the file is unencrypted (see OPEN_POINTS.md 1.3/1.4).
config.erasure: /forget deletes the chat's transcript and api_requests rows (not scrubbed until VACUUM); no time-based retention for transcripts

nodes.name: API request log
nodes.description: Table api_requests: append-only log of Picnic and OpenRouter calls, including prompts, tool results and order data in the bodies. Sensitive.

api-log-consent.description: A chat that opted out of history gets rows without bodies or URL query strings. /forget, /privacy off, delete_turns and delete_day delete the chat's rows in the same transaction.

config.name: API log follows history consent
config.description: A chat that opted out of history gets rows without bodies or URL query strings. /forget, /privacy off, delete_turns and delete_day delete the chat's rows in the same transaction.
config.erasure: Rows carry chat_id and are deleted with the chat's turns; older rows pruned after API_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS by each import run
config.failure-mode: fail-closed: no bodies when consent cannot be confirmed
config.enforced-in: src/picnic_meal_planner/bot.py::_run_llm (request_context store_bodies), api_log.py::_may_store_bodies, history.py deletion paths

nodes.name: Chat settings
nodes.description: Table chat_settings: per-chat persist_history flag and model (NULL = LLM_MODEL).

nodes.name: Picnic session token
nodes.description: Table picnic_auth (one row): the Picnic session token every process starts from.

credential-handling.description: Never logged in clear: api_log masks x-picnic-auth. Cleared only if it is still the stored one, so a fresh login from another process is never wiped. Stored in plain text in the SQLite file.

config.name: Picnic session token handling
config.description: Never logged in clear: api_log masks x-picnic-auth. Cleared only if it is still the stored one, so a fresh login from another process is never wiped. Stored in plain text in the SQLite file.
config.erasure: Cleared when Picnic rejects it, only if it is still the stored token

nodes.name: History import script
nodes.description: Re-runnable, rate-limit-safe import of past Picnic deliveries into orders/order_items, then a category backfill for products without a category_id, L1/L2 name lookups and a capped refresh of stale names (each skipped once Picnic rate limits past the backoff), then prunes the API log. Idle runs write no orders or checkpoints.

nodes.name: Picnic login script
nodes.description: Interactive shell front end for the same LoginFlow as /picnic_login (password + 2FA); stores the session token. --status checks the stored session.

nodes.name: Chat model script
nodes.description: List / set / reset a chat's LLM model through llm.set_chat_model (honours LLM_ALLOWED_MODELS).

nodes.name: Category inspection script
nodes.description: Diagnostic: prints or saves the outline of a product's category pages, to check a parser against a real payload. Read-only apart from refreshing the session token.

nodes.name: Preflight check
nodes.description: Checks configuration and, unless --offline, makes live calls to OpenRouter, Telegram and Picnic before the bot is started. Never prints secrets.

nodes.name: Reporting web app
nodes.description: FastAPI app (`uv run web`): read-only reports over the order history, redeeming the one-time login links /report hands out, and the built frontend from the same origin. Aggregation is pure Python in web/reports.py. Refuses to start when the schema is behind.

report-session.description: Every /api route except the login needs a signed session cookie, and the Telegram allowlist is checked again on each request, so removing a user ends their session at once.

config.name: Report session and allowlist
config.description: Every /api route except the login needs a signed session cookie, and the Telegram allowlist is checked again on each request, so removing a user ends their session at once.
config.allowed-principals: Telegram user ids in ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS holding a session cookie

local-only-listener.description: The web app binds 127.0.0.1 unless WEB_HOST says otherwise. It is not part of the container image or the compose file.

config.name: Reports listen on localhost
config.description: The web app binds 127.0.0.1 unless WEB_HOST says otherwise. It is not part of the container image or the compose file.

reports-read-only-scope.description: The web app reads orders, order lines, products and categories. It never reads conversations, the API request log or the Picnic token, and writes nothing but login tokens.

config.name: Reports read order data only
config.description: The web app reads orders, order lines, products and categories. It never reads conversations, the API request log or the Picnic token, and writes nothing but login tokens.

nodes.name: Reporting frontend
nodes.description: React single-page app in the browser: category tree, orders-over-time chart and login page. Built with Vite, shadcn/ui, Recharts, TanStack Query and Router. The selected node, interval and date range live in the URL.

nodes.name: Report login tokens
nodes.description: Table web_login_tokens: SHA-256 hashes of the one-time login links, with user id, expiry and time of use.

one-time-login-links.description: A link's token is random, stored only as a hash, valid for 5 minutes and consumed by a single UPDATE on first use. It travels in the URL fragment, which is not sent to the server.

config.name: One-time login links
config.description: A link's token is random, stored only as a hash, valid for 5 minutes and consumed by a single UPDATE on first use. It travels in the URL fragment, which is not sent to the server.
config.erasure: Expired rows are deleted whenever a new link is created
config.failure-mode: Creating or redeeming propagates errors, a login never succeeds unverified

flows.name: Answer a chat message with tools
flows.description: One free-text message: context in, LLM with tool rounds, tools against Picnic and the DB, clean turn archived.

transitions.description: A family member sends a message in Telegram.
The bot receives the update by long polling and checks the allowlist.
A request_context is opened for the turn: bodies are logged only if the chat consents to history.
history.get_context() returns the cached or DB-loaded window of whole turns.
On a cold cache, load_recent_turns() reads the newest whole turns.
The chat's model is resolved and create_message() is called with tools.
chat_settings.model is read (NULL means LLM_MODEL).
History is translated to OpenAI format and sent, and the reply is translated back.
The OpenRouter request and completion are logged with the key masked.
The row is written on the log engine and a lock costs the row, not the request.
Each tool_use is executed with call_tool() and its result goes back as a tool_result.
e.g. search_products / add_to_cart go to the Picnic client.
The Picnic API is called with the stored session token.
The captured Picnic HTTP calls are logged with x-picnic-auth masked.
History tools and the product cache read and write the local DB.
Forecast tools rank products by urgency.
Loop: the conversation including tool results goes back to the model until it stops.
commit_turn() archives the turn if it ended cleanly.
append_turn() writes all messages of the turn under one turn_id.
The reply is sent, split into 4096-character chunks.

flows.name: Import Picnic delivery history
flows.description: scripts/import_history.py: work list = deliveries with no row in orders; batched, re-runnable.

transitions.description: The operator (or a schedule) runs the import script.
The run opens request_context with source import_history and one run_id.
All delivery summaries are fetched, then each new delivery's detail.
python-picnic-api2 calls Picnic, pausing IMPORT_DELAY_SECONDS between batches.
Orders, line items and products are inserted, and a checkpoint is logged per batch.
Rows are committed to SQLite.

Category backfill: get_category_ids for products without a category_id, get_l3_names once per unknown L3, get_l1_names per L1 with a name missing or due a retry/refresh, and get_l3_names per L2 page due a refresh, at most CATEGORY_REFRESH_LIMIT per run. A rate limit backs off and retries.
upsert_category stores every L3 named on the page, set_product_category links the product, upsert_category_parent stores the L1 and L2 names, and checked_at records when each name was confirmed.
prune_expired deletes api_requests rows older than API_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS.

flows.name: Log in to Picnic over Telegram
flows.description: Recovering from PicnicLoginRequired: password login, 2FA code, token stored for every process.

transitions.description: An authorised user sends /picnic_login [sms|email].
The bot receives the command and checks PICNIC_LOGIN_USER_IDS.
start_login() runs LoginFlow.start().
Password login. On 2FA Picnic sends the owner a code and the login stays pending for 10 minutes.
The user sends /picnic_code with the code, which calls submit_login_code() on the same pending PicnicAPI.
The code is verified and Picnic returns a session token.
The token is saved to picnic_auth for the bot, scripts and MCP server.
The operator triggers the Build & Deploy workflow.
The runtime image is built and pushed to GHCR.
The workflow SSHes into the VPS and runs docker compose.
The VPS pulls :latest and recreates the container.

flows.name: Open the order reports
flows.description: From /report in Telegram to a drill-down chart in the browser.

transitions.description: An authorised user sends /report in their private chat.
The bot checks the allowlist and refuses group chats.
create_login_link stores the token's hash with a 5 minute expiry and the bot replies with the link.
The user opens the link. The login page takes the token out of the address bar and waits for a click.
The page posts the token to /api/auth/login.
The token is consumed once, the allowlist is checked again, and a signed session cookie is set.
The page loads the category tree and the time series with the cookie.
Orders, order lines, products and categories are read and aggregated.
